Define a hybrid (deep-neural-network) demographic process for FINN

Source: R/Processes_utils.R
createHybrid.Rd

Configures a process (growth, mortality, or regeneration) in which the entire process equation – not just its environmental-response function – is replaced by a deep neural network (DNN), for use as growth_process, mortality_process, or regeneration_process in finn(). This is the second ("Level 2") level of hybridization described by Pichler & Käber (2026); to replace only the environmental-response function while keeping the rest of the process mechanistic ("Level 1"), use createProcess() instead. competition_process must always be created with createProcess(), as the competition (light availability) process does not support full replacement by a DNN.

Usage

createHybrid(
  formula = NULL,
  optimize = TRUE,
  dispersion_parameter = 1,
  NN = NULL,
  dropout = 0.3,
  encoder_layers = 1L,
  hidden = c(50L, 50L),
  sample_regeneration = TRUE,
  transformer = TRUE,
  emb_dim = 20L,
  dim_feedforward = 256L,
  mortality_draw = c("binomial", "bernoulli", "poisson", "gamma"),
  regeneration_sampler = c("refined", "gaussian"),
  cap = c("all", "species"),
  prior = "max_obs_recruits",
  prior_lambda = 0.1,
  theta_floor = 0.5,
  optimizeTheta = TRUE,
  mortality_floor = 0.001,
  mortality_ceiling = 0.999
)

Arguments

formula

(formula)
Environmental predictors passed to the network, evaluated against the env data. Default NULL uses ~. (all available environmental covariates).

optimize

(logical(1))
Should the network's weights be estimated during fit()? Default TRUE.

dispersion_parameter

(numeric(1))
Initial dispersion parameter of the negative binomial distribution used to sample recruits, or its fixed value with optimizeTheta = FALSE. Only used when this object is the regeneration process. See recruitment.

NN

(nn_module)
Not supported in 0.2.0. A custom module was accepted and then ignored, so a non-NULL value now raises an error; shape the default network with hidden, dropout and transformer instead.

dropout

(numeric(1))
Dropout rate of the network. Default 0.3; the Barro Colorado Island case study of Pichler & Käber (2026) used 0.1.

encoder_layers

(integer(1))
Number of transformer encoder layers. Only used when transformer = TRUE.

hidden

(integer())
Hidden-layer sizes of the feed-forward network. Only used when transformer = FALSE.

sample_regeneration

(logical(1))
Should recruits actually be sampled from the negative binomial regeneration distribution (TRUE), or only its expectation used (FALSE)? Only used when this object is the regeneration process. With FALSE the expected number of recruits per patch is rounded, so wherever it is below 0.5 no recruit enters at all. See recruitment.

transformer

(logical(1))
Use a transformer encoder architecture (TRUE, default) or a feed-forward network (FALSE).

emb_dim

(integer(1))
Embedding dimension for the species/cohort/ environment features.

dim_feedforward

(integer(1))
Dimension of the feed-forward sublayer within each transformer encoder layer. Only used when transformer = TRUE.

mortality_draw

(character(1))
How the number of dead trees is drawn, "binomial" (default since 0.2.0), "bernoulli", "poisson" or "gamma"; see createProcess(). Only used when this object is the mortality process.

regeneration_sampler

(character(1))
How recruits are drawn, "refined" (default since 0.2.0) or "gaussian"; see createProcess(). Only used when this object is the regeneration process.

cap, prior, prior_lambda

Accepted for symmetry with createProcess(), but not used in 0.2.0: the hybrid regeneration network has no Beverton-Holt cap. See regeneration_capped() for the cap of the mechanistic process.

theta_floor

(numeric(1))
Lower bound on the recruit dispersion par_theta_recruits, default 0.5 since 0.2.0, 0 or NULL to leave it unbounded as in 0.1.0; see createProcess(). Only used when this object is the regeneration process. The floor keeps the fit stable. In one converged pair of fits on the German national forest inventory it calibrated the recruitment level as well as a fixed theta, but only after the parameters had settled; read the level once $param_history shows them settled, or fix theta (optimizeTheta = FALSE) for short fits. See recruitment.

optimizeTheta

(logical(1))
Should the recruit dispersion be estimated during fit()? Default TRUE; FALSE keeps it at dispersion_parameter, which is the choice when the recruitment level is to be calibrated; see createProcess() and recruitment. Only used when this object is the regeneration process.

mortality_floor, mortality_ceiling

(numeric(1))
The interval the mortality probability is clamped to per simulation step before the death draw, defaults 0.001 and 0.999; see createProcess(). Only used when this object is the mortality process.

Value

A list of class "hybrid" containing the process definition and associated parameters, to be passed as growth_process, mortality_process, or regeneration_process to finn().

Details

The network receives the same cohort- and site-level information that the corresponding mechanistic process equation would use – diameter at breast height, number of trees, available light, species identity and the site's environmental predictors (plus the growth rate, for the mortality process) – and predicts the process output directly. Species identity is passed through a learned embedding layer rather than treated as a categorical covariate with per-species coefficients, so the network can learn low-dimensional "contrasts" between species or plant functional types (PFTs). An inverse-link function appropriate to each process is applied to the network's output: a sigmoid for mortality (a per-tree death probability, as for mortality), and an exponential for growth and regeneration (always-positive rates; for regeneration this is the mean of the negative binomial distribution from which recruits are drawn, as for regeneration).

Two network architectures are available, selected with transformer. The default (transformer = TRUE) is a small transformer encoder (encoder_layers layers, embedding dimension emb_dim, feed-forward dimension dim_feedforward) that embeds each cohort, its species and the site's environment and attends across the cohorts of a patch. Setting transformer = FALSE instead uses a feed-forward network with hidden layers hidden (default two layers of 50 units each) and dropout, matching the architecture used by Pichler & Käber (2026) for the Barro Colorado Island case study (where dropout was set to 10%).

As with createProcess(), hybrid processes are calibrated jointly, end-to-end, with the remaining mechanistic or hybrid processes via fit(), rather than pre-trained in isolation and plugged in afterwards. optimize controls whether the network's weights are estimated during fitting or kept fixed at their (random) initial values, and dispersion_parameter/ sample_regeneration have the same meaning as in createProcess() and are only used when this object is the regeneration process.

References

Pichler, M., & Käber, Y. (2026). Inferring processes within dynamic forest models using hybrid modelling. Methods in Ecology and Evolution. doi:10.1111/2041-210x.70347

See also

createProcess(), finn(), recruitment

Examples

# A hybrid process is a recipe, like createProcess(): no data and no torch
# are needed until the model is built. The default network is a small
# transformer encoder
growth_process <- createHybrid(formula = ~ temp + prec)
class(growth_process)
#> [1] "hybrid"

# a feed-forward network with two hidden layers instead, as in the Barro
# Colorado Island case study of the paper
mortality_process <- createHybrid(~ temp + prec, transformer = FALSE,
                                  hidden = c(50L, 50L), dropout = 0.1)

library(data.table)
# a model whose growth is a network while mortality, regeneration and
# competition stay mechanistic, fitted for two epochs on three sites of the
# bundled Oregon FIA data (?fia_obs_dt)
sites <- 1:3
Nsp   <- max(fia_obs_dt$species)
init  <- makeInitCohorts(fia_init_trees[siteID %in% sites], Nspecies = Nsp)
FINN.seed(1)
m <- finn(N_species = Nsp, recruits_dbh = 12.9,
          growth_process       = createHybrid(~ temp + prec, transformer = FALSE,
                                              hidden = c(16L, 16L), dropout = 0.1),
          mortality_process    = createProcess(~ temp + prec, mortality),
          regeneration_process = createProcess(~ temp + prec, regeneration_capped))
fit(m, data = fia_obs_dt[siteID %in% sites], env = fia_env_dt[siteID %in% sites],
    init_cohort = init, epochs = 2L, patches = 4, patch_size = 0.06,
    plot_progress = FALSE)
#> ℹ weights: intercept-only baseline x your vector (dbh=0.00243, ba=12, trees=0.968, growth=1.84e+04, mortality=38.5, regeneration=0.768)
#> ℹ share of the objective at the intercept-only baseline (scaled): dbh=17%, ba=17%, trees=17%, growth=17%, mortality=17%, regeneration=17%
# the network takes the place of the growth equation in the simulation
sim <- simulateForest(m, env = fia_env_dt[siteID %in% sites], init_cohort = init)
head(sim$long$site[variable == "growth" & year == 10 & value > 0])
#>    siteID  year species variable      value
#>     <int> <int>   <int>   <fctr>      <num>
#> 1:      1    10       1   growth 0.03613109
#> 2:      1    10       3   growth 0.04689414
#> 3:      1    10       4   growth 0.04193100
#> 4:      1    10       5   growth 0.03449138
#> 5:      1    10       6   growth 0.05649123
#> 6:      1    10      11   growth 0.03411257
